Clinical History writeup: Mrs. Riddhi Kothari and Mr. Karan Desai are a non-consanguineous couple. Their first pregnancy resulted in a missed abortion at 10 weeks of gestation. The second pregnancy was terminated following the identification of multiple congenital anomalies on prenatal evaluation, including an extended spine, flexion at the elbows with fisted hands, extended knees with rocker-bottom feet, and high-resistance flow in both uterine arteries, raising a suspicion of fetal akinesia. Fetal radiographs revealed minimally curved femora, irregular metaphyses, and a dysplastic pelvis. Fetal autopsy findings were consistent with an arthrogryposis phenotype, showing fixed contractures, extension contractures at both knees, flexion contractures at both elbows, overlapping fingers, rocker-bottom and malrotated feet, poorly formed and atrophic leg muscles, bilateral proptosis, microretrognathia, and an abnormally shaped skull. Enhanced whole exome sequencing and mitochondrial genome sequencing performed on the products of conception (done elsewhere) identified a homozygous variant of uncertain significance, c.1292-1G>C, in the NUP88 gene, which is associated with Fetal Akinesia Deformation Sequence 4 (FADS4). Carrier screening of the couple by Sanger sequencing for the NUP88 gene (done elsewhere) revealed that both partners are heterozygous carriers for the same variant (c.1292-1G>C). Additional carrier screening for Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA) by deletion/duplication analysis (done elsewhere) showed that the female partner carries a heterozygous duplication of exons 7 and 8 in the SMN1 gene and a heterozygous deletion of exons 7 and 8 in the SMN2 gene, while the male partner showed no deletion or duplication in either SMN1 or SMN2 genes. There is a significant family history on the male partner’s side, with his mother diagnosed with breast cancer at 48 years and cervical cancer at 59 years, and his maternal grandmother diagnosed with breast and  cervical cancer in her 80s. Mrs. Riddhi Kothari and Mr. Karan Desai have been evaluated for pathogenic variations.
